audits.title: An audit of the quality of root canal treatments performed by undergraduate dental students on single-rooted teeth in Glasgow dental hospital and school.
audits.standard: Predetermined radiographic criteria for acceptable root canal filling
audits.setting: Glasgow Dental Hospital and School (undergraduate student treatments)

cycle1.result: Of 100 teeth, 20 had voids and one was perforated; of the remaining 79, 80% (n=63) acceptable, 5% (n=4) under-filled and 15% (n=12) over-filled.

audits.other_findings: Quality judged comparable to or better than other international institutions.
audits.citation: Pettigrew LK, Jauhar S, Lynch CD, Savarrio L, Carrotte P, Hannigan A. An audit of the quality of root canal treatments performed by undergraduate dental students on single-rooted teeth in Glasgow dental hospital and school. Eur J Prosthodont Restor Dent. 2007;15(2):72-76. PMID: 17645068.

audits.title: Radiographic evaluation of the technical quality of undergraduate endodontic 'competence' cases in the Dublin Dental University Hospital: an audit.
audits.standard: European guidelines for technical quality of root canal treatment (obturation within 2 mm of apex, no voids or errors)
audits.setting: Undergraduate endodontic competence cases, Dublin Dental University Hospital

cycle1.result: Acceptable: 49% of single-rooted and 17% of multi-rooted teeth; voids in 36% (single) and 38% (multi); within 2 mm of apex 69% and 60%.

audits.other_findings: 119 canals in 78 teeth selected; five teeth excluded for missing or non-diagnostic radiographs; results similar to previous undergraduate studies.
audits.citation: Kumar M, Duncan HF. Radiographic evaluation of the technical quality of undergraduate endodontic 'competence' cases in the Dublin Dental University Hospital: an audit. J Ir Dent Assoc. 2012;58(3):162-166. PMID: 22888740.

audits.title: A re-audit of the technical quality of undergraduate root canal treatment after the introduction of new technology and teaching practices.
audits.standard: Four radiographic criteria: no voids, filling termination 0-2 mm of apex, all roots filled, original anatomy maintained

cycle1.result: Acceptable fillings in 48% of single-rooted and 38% of multirooted canals; 18.8% of multirooted teeth acceptable as a unit.

audits.intervention: Educational changes and mandatory new technologies (nickel-titanium files, apex locators, greater taper gutta-percha).

cycle2.result: Acceptable in 23/40 (57.5%) single-rooted and 68/129 (52.7%) multirooted canals; 45.2% of multirooted teeth acceptable (P = 0.042).

audits.other_findings: Voids and unsatisfactory termination fell by 23% and 14% in multirooted and 11% and 12% in single-rooted teeth.
audits.citation: Donnelly A, Coffey D, Duncan HF. A re-audit of the technical quality of undergraduate root canal treatment after the introduction of new technology and teaching practices. Int Endod J. 2017;50(10):941-950. doi:10.1111/iej.12727. PMID: 27917512.

audits.title: Clinical audit training improves undergraduates' performance in root canal therapy.
audits.standard: Published record keeping guidelines and root canal technical quality criteria
audits.setting: School of Dentistry, International Medical University, Kuala Lumpur (undergraduate clinics)

cycle1.result: Record keeping compliance 44.1%; 44.7% of root canal fillings met all 3 technical quality criteria.

audits.intervention: Clinical audit-feedback cycle: findings reported in class with recommendations for improvement.

cycle2.result: Record keeping compliance 94.6% (P = .001); 76.8% of root canal fillings met all 3 criteria (P = .001).

audits.other_findings: Interim 2014 audit: record keeping 79.6% and 48.6% met all criteria.
audits.citation: Fong JYM, Tan VJH, Lee JR, Tong ZGM, Foong YK, Tan JME, et al.. Clinical audit training improves undergraduates' performance in root canal therapy. Eur J Dent Educ. 2018;22(3):160-166. doi:10.1111/eje.12297. PMID: 29266663.

audits.title: An audit of root canal filling quality performed by undergraduate pre-clinical dental students, Yemen.
audits.standard: Radiographic quality criteria for root canal fillings (length, density and taper)
audits.setting: Faculty of Dentistry, Thamar University (pre-clinical undergraduate teaching)

cycle1.result: Of 741 roots in 331 extracted teeth: adequate length 53.4%, adequate density 13.1%, adequate taper 14.2%; overall quality poor.

audits.other_findings: Anterior and single-rooted teeth had significantly better quality than posterior and multi-rooted teeth; mandibular better than maxillary but not significant (P > 0.05).
audits.citation: Al-Anesi MS, AlKhawlani MM, Alkheraif AA, Al-Basmi AA, Alhajj MN. An audit of root canal filling quality performed by undergraduate pre-clinical dental students, Yemen. BMC Med Educ. 2019;19(1):350. doi:10.1186/s12909-019-1798-1. PMID: 31519180.

audits.title: Is there a justification of conducting clinical audit in the endodontic treatment outcomes?
audits.standard: Evidence-based endodontic treatment and success predictors (audit tool)
audits.setting: Department of endodontics, dental specialty centre (retrospective record review of 12 months)

cycle1.result: Vitality test recorded in 1.98% of cases; intracanal medicament used and named in 3.96%; 3.96% of teeth extracted for endodontic failure; 6.93% had voids but root canal filling overall satisfactory.

audits.other_findings: Vitality testing, medicament type and root filling assessment were largely not documented.
audits.citation: Karobari MI, Khijmatgar S, Noorani TY, Assiry A, Alharbi T. Is there a justification of conducting clinical audit in the endodontic treatment outcomes?. J Conserv Dent. 2020;23(5):518-521. doi:10.4103/jcd.jcd_220_19. PMID: 33911363.

audits.title: An Audit of the Technical Quality and Iatrogenic Errors of Root Canal Treatment by Undergraduate Dental Students at the University of Sharjah.
audits.standard: Acceptable root filling: adequate length, density and taper with no iatrogenic errors
audits.setting: College of Dental Medicine, University of Sharjah (undergraduate student clinics)

cycle1.result: Acceptable quality in 183/480 teeth (38.1%); 4th-year students 41.9% vs 5th-year 27.4% (p = 0.004).

audits.other_findings: Length and taper adequate more often in teeth treated by 4th-year students.
audits.citation: Al Shehadat S, El-Kishawi M, AlMudalal A, AlSaqer A, Nassar A, Zihlif L, et al.. An Audit of the Technical Quality and Iatrogenic Errors of Root Canal Treatment by Undergraduate Dental Students at the University of Sharjah. Eur J Dent. 2023;17(1):191-199. doi:10.1055/s-0042-1743150. PMID: 35279818.

audits.title: Retrospective audit for quality assessment of root fillings performed by undergraduate dental students in clinics.
audits.standard: Standardised criteria for obturation length, density and taper
audits.setting: Undergraduate dental clinics, College of Dentistry, Qassim University

cycle1.result: 80.2% of 653 canals (397 teeth, 347 patients) acceptable on all three criteria.

audits.other_findings: Length control was the most frequent deficiency; maxillary teeth better than mandibular; mesio-lingual canal poorest.
audits.citation: Javed MQ, AlAttas MH, Bhatti UA, Dutta SD. Retrospective audit for quality assessment of root fillings performed by undergraduate dental students in clinics. J Taibah Univ Med Sci. 2022;17(2):297-303. doi:10.1016/j.jtumed.2021.10.005. PMID: 35592806.

audits.title: Quality of endodontic record-keeping and root canal obturation performed by final year undergraduate dental students: An audit during the COVID-19 pandemic.
audits.standard: European Society of Endodontology guidelines for record-keeping and root canal obturation
audits.setting: Undergraduate dental clinics, AIMST University, Kedah

cycle1.result: 78 (70.3%) root fillings satisfactory; endodontic treatment records had the lowest documentation rates.

audits.other_findings: No difference in filling quality between anterior and posterior or maxillary and mandibular teeth.
audits.citation: Lin GSS, Tan WW, Chan DZK, Chua KH, Yee TC, Lazaldin MAM. Quality of endodontic record-keeping and root canal obturation performed by final year undergraduate dental students: An audit during the COVID-19 pandemic. PLoS One. 2022;17(10):e0275634. doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0275634. PMID: 36191029.
